matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: When the numeric discrepancy between the two sides of the equation is a multiple of 1, try moving a single vertical stick (the I) from one numeral to another to adjust the values.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the difference in total values can be resolved by adding or removing a value of 1 (i.e., by adding or removing an I).
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from a numeral that leaves the source numeral without any I's, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character; common intra‑character transformations (e.g., V→X, X→V, plus→minus) often resolve the puzzle.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick move could change a character into another valid Roman numeral or operator without affecting other characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V but leaving a single diagonal stick, which yields an invalid character.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, verify that each resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or allowed operator; discard transformations that produce invalid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick move, before checking arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Creating 'VVIII', which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; when moving a diagonal from X or V, ensure you do not leave a lone angled stick behind.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is moved from a character composed of diagonals.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign, which is a valid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and changing it to minus may help balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from a plus but not placing it elsewhere, leaving an extra stray stick.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a vertical stick to create an extra I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When there is a spare stick after a transformation and forming a new numeral could adjust the values.
matchstick.example: Leaving a detached stick unused instead of forming a new numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If intra‑character moves fail, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character, such as from a numeral to an operator or vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a numeral to another numeral and leaving the source invalid.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting '+' to '-', the freed vertical stick can be attached to a nearby numeral to increase its value (e.g., turning I into II).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is turned into a minus and the vertical stick can be used to augment a numeral.
matchstick.example: Failing to attach the freed vertical stick, leaving it unused.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of the left‑hand side and right‑hand side after any transformation; ensure the equation holds true.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After a candidate transformation passes symbol validation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Proposing 'VII - XVIII + VI', which does not satisfy the equality.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the '=', ensure the final equation still contains a valid '=' sign (e.g., by converting another operator into '='); do not eliminate the equality sign entirely.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a horizontal stick from '=', verify that another operator can become '=' to maintain the equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '=' and ending up with no '=' sign in the equation.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to consider moving sticks between characters first, missing simpler fixes that stay within a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always attempt intra‑character stick relocations (e.g., V→X, X→V) before exploring inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a diagonal without repositioning it, leaving an isolated angled stick that doesn't form a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a diagonal from X or V, ensure the remaining sticks still form a valid numeral, or reposition the removed diagonal to create another valid character.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual validity of symbols and forgets to check whether the resulting equation is mathematically correct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After a transformation passes symbol validation, compute the numeric values of both sides and confirm the equality before accepting the solution.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operators as interchangeable and neglects the requirement that the final equation must contain exactly one equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When modifying operators, verify that the final equation still includes a single, valid '=' sign.

matchstick.description: Forgetting to place the removed stick after modifying an operator (e.g., converting plus to minus) and leaving it unused
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from an operator but does not attach it elsewhere, violating the rule that sticks must be relocated, not discarded.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After converting an operator (e.g., '+' to '-'), immediately use the freed stick to augment another numeral or form a new valid character.
